items.note: Dikshit's conjecture that Siyaka, in invading the Rāshṭrakūṭa capital about 973 A.C., took the earlier Rāshṭrakūṭa grant plate as booty, later reused by Vākpati.
Gaonrī grant: Vākpatirājadeva donates the village Vaṇikā in Hūṇa-maṇḍala to thirty-six Brāhmaṇas.
Donees hailed to Mālwā from Magadha, Dakshina-Rāḍha, Uttara-Kula, Sāvathika, Lāta and Madhyadēśa, valuable for the social history of Mālwā of this period.
Genealogy in the Gaonrī grant: Krishnarāja, successor Vairisiṃha, successor Siyaka, all of the Paramāra house of Mālwā, predecessors of Vākpatirājadeva.
According to the Udaipur praśasti, Vākpati's father Siyaka defeated the Hūnas.
